build.summary:
I built proc-tip-context. The full case now has a tips panel in the right column, under the haemodynamic monitor. It merges access, diagnostic, PCI and haemodynamic tips through one pure context function. caseTipContexts(session, workspace, stage) builds one context per lab for each workspace, following the plan's table. In the access workspace it reports the current step and the site together: puncture until the wire runs free, wire while the wire is at the needle, sheath from needle removal until the sheath is flushed.

CaseSession gained accessStep(), activeEvents() and noteTipsShown(), and its summary now carries tipsShown. activeEvents() reads an EventLog on the patient clock. That log holds:
- events the session raises from what the operator sees or feels: venous-flashback, no-flashback, radial-spasm, radial-loop, perforation, bleeding, haematoma, pressure-damped, air
- patient events from the shared adapter, sampled from the vitals at most once per second
- scenario and module events

selectCaseTips() applies a cap per lab and a total cap. At an access step it also leaves out tips written for another step at the same site, and ranks tips for the current step first, so wire and sheath tips do not crowd the puncture. caseTips.ts exports raises for the reachability report.

The PCI and haemodynamic contexts get only patient and scenario events, so an arm perforation never brings up a coronary perforation tip. In the reachability report the access lab went from 5 to 85 satisfiable tips out of 89. 85 of the 87 waiting tips naming this package are now satisfiable; the 2 cold-leg tips are not (see criteria).

The dev hook __caseSession.tips() is async. It returns the mode, whether tips are visible, the workspace, stage, step, events, contexts, the panel's ids and the tips shown so far.

After the flush the step is null, and the table workspace still reports phase sheath. Test 'a radial session never yields a femoral-only tip': at the chart, puncture, wire, sheath and after heparin, across all 7 workspaces, no tip whose route excludes radial appears, either in tipsFor(ctx, 1000) over every context or in the panel.

A real radial puncture taken through the back wall raises no-flashback, and tipsFor(ctx, 20) includes access-needle-flashback-check. access-central-vein-no-blood needs route jugular or subclavian, and the full case has no such site (AccessRoute is femoral, radial-right or radial-left). Of the 87 waiting tips naming this package, 85 are now satisfiable (2 of them were already reachable through a diagnostic borrow). The access lab count went from 5 to 85 of 89. The 2 cold-leg tips are not satisfiable: access-cx-cold-leg-six-ps and access-closure-cold-leg need limb-ischaemia, which only a scenario script raises in the full case. The panel caps CASE_TIP_LIMITS, CASE_TIP_LIMITS_AT_ACCESS and STEP_BONUS in caseTips.ts are display settings, not clinical values.

build.notes:
I snapshotted the two existing files (caseSession.ts and ProcedureLab.tsx) before editing, into datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/proc-tip-context/ with their relative paths, and created .started. The other three listed files are new.

Design choices to check:
1. caseSession.ts now imports two framework-free modules from ui/lab: EventLog and PatientEventAdapter/PATIENT_EVENTS. This puts a value import from ui into simulation. Without it the session could not hold the 10 s hypotension window on its own clock.
2. The tip log runs on the patient clock, because the adapter raises at vitals.t. Telemetry 'lab.event' rows carry tWall = session time.
3. Retroperitoneal bleeds raise no 'bleeding'. Their cue is the hypotension the adapter raises, so the tip context never names the cause. The nurse-reported groin and forearm swellings and pseudoaneurysm hold 'haematoma'; a rebleed raises 'bleeding'.
4. The ACT feeds 'low-act' only once the case has gone to PCI, because the adapter's ACT goal is the PCI goal.
5. caseTips.ts imports caseSession.ts as a value (for CASE_SESSION_EVENTS and CASE_PATIENT_EVENTS), so the declaration cannot drift from what the session raises. The reachability test therefore loads the session module; it still runs in milliseconds.
6. The step filter and step bonus are a selection rule in caseTips.ts only; tips.ts is unchanged. Without them, femoral wire and sheath caution tips pushed access-femoral-scan-bifurcation out of the puncture panel.
7. When the case is handed to the diagnostic or PCI lab, caseTipContexts returns no context, since that lab shows its own tips.
8. One test sets the wire's perforation flag directly to simulate a forced hydrophilic wire. The hypotension test overrides engine.vitals so that it returns a fixed low cuff reading.

The whole suite was not run, per the machine limits; only the files listed above were.

review.verdict: Mostly complete and sound. The package needs one fix before it can be accepted. Checks: both test files pass (17/17), reachability.test.ts and caseSession.test.ts pass (19/19), and tsc -p tsconfig.app.json is clean. I tested the browser criterion myself in a background tab of the running dev server. __caseSession.tips() for a guided femoral case at the access workspace (step puncture) listed access-femoral-scan-bifurcation, though only 8th of 8. In exam mode, even after askHelp, it returned visible=false and ids=[], and no Tips panel was rendered. I diffed the snapshots: caseSession.ts and ProcedureLab.tsx change only as the report describes. Every other file under src/ newer than .started belongs to another package's file list (haemo-study-session-and-tips, pci-device-catalogue, pci-scenario-registry), or is a new test beside one of them. Shared engines keep their defaults: tips.ts, eventLog.ts and patientEvents.ts are unchanged and the adapter's thresholds are unchanged. The per-frame path is clean: sampleTipEvents returns early on the 1 s gate, and the panel recomputes at the 8 Hz re-render using a JSON key. Labs this package does not touch behave as before. The panel uses its own selectCaseTips rather than useContextTips. That is an acceptable deviation, because per-lab caps cannot be expressed through useContextTips' single limit. The blocking defect: a radial case can still show a femoral-only tip. Contexts outside the access workspace carry no site phase, and the test defines 'femoral-only' by `route` alone, so it misses this. The other findings are minor ground-truth and coverage gaps, plus out-of-scope items the builder correctly reported.

findings.problem: A radial session can show a femoral-only tip, breaking acceptance criterion 1. The chart, fluoro, table and closure contexts carry no site phase (access('sheath') with route 'radial'). tipScore matches phases as a union, so a tip whose trigger is phase [stage, 'femoral'] with no route still matches. Reproduced: radial-right session, start 'sheath-in', wire perforation, table workspace. The panel shows access-sheath-ooze-upsize ('Bleeding around a femoral sheath: upsize it', when {phase:['sheath','femoral'], event:['bleeding']}). The radial chart also shows access-planning-hostile-groin ({phase:['plan','femoral']}). In the other direction, access-radial-spasm-no-traction matches femoral closure and complication contexts if radial-spasm is ever active. The test misses this because femoralOnly checks only when.route.

radial-spasm is raised from the hidden model level wire.spasm >= 0.5, sampled every second. Spasm also builds from anxiety in slowTick while the wire is still. The spasm tips (verapamil, no traction) can therefore appear before the operator has any cue: no wire move, no pain, no 'spasm' wire event (that fires at 0.75). This contradicts the file's own rule, 'never from a hidden diagnosis'.
findings.fix: Delete `const armWire = ...; if (armWire && this.wire.spasm >= MP_TIPS.spasmLevel) this.raiseTip("radial-spasm");` from sampleTipEvents. In commandWire, after `this.spasmSeen = Math.max(...)`, add `if (this.access !== "femoral" && advance !== 0 && this.wire.spasm >= MP_TIPS.spasmLevel) this.raiseTip("radial-spasm");`. That is the felt resistance on a move; the spasm event and the patient's pain stay as they are. Add a test: a radial session with the wire in the arm, high anxiety and no moves raises no radial-spasm.

findings.problem: no-flashback is raised only after a 'back-wall' puncture event, which is hidden model state. With no blood at the hub, the operator cannot tell a needle short of the artery from one that has gone through it. The event, shown in the DEV row and used by any future no-flashback tip, therefore reveals which one it is. No case-reachable tip uses it yet (access-central-vein-no-blood needs jugular or subclavian), so the impact today is small.
findings.fix: Replace passBackWall with what the operator sees: a flashback that was there and has stopped. Rename it to passHadFlash. Reset it to false on 'skin-pass'. In hubTipEvents, set it to true when f.kind !== 'none'. Raise 'no-flashback' when f.kind === 'none' && this.passHadFlash. Remove the `this.passBackWall = true` in the back-wall case. Keep the wire-resistance 'no-lumen' raise. The existing back-wall test still passes, because the flash is seen first.

findings.problem: The design lists high-contrast-volume, and the adapter raises it only from the engine's own contrast total (v.contrast.fractionOfMacd). When the diagnostic or PCI lab returns with returnFromLab({contrastMl, ...}) and patientAdvanced is not set, that contrast goes into labTotals, not the engine. A case that used most of its maximum contrast dose in angiography therefore never raises high-contrast-volume at closure or recovery.
findings.fix: Construct the adapter with a ceiling check that includes the lab totals: `private readonly patientTipEvents = new PatientEventAdapter(this.tipEvents, { contrastHigh: (c) => c.totalMl + this.labTotals.contrastMl >= PATIENT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS.contrastFraction * this.profile.renal.macdMl });`. Import PATIENT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS from ../../ui/lab/patientEvents. Add a test: returnFromLab('diagnostic', { contrastMl: 0.9 * macdMl, fluoroS: 100 }), then wait(2), then activeEvents() contains high-contrast-volume.

findings.where: src/ui/access/caseTips.ts STEP_BONUS and CASE_TIP_LIMITS_AT_ACCESS; header lines 36-41
findings.problem: The header says tips of the current step rank before tips of the site alone, but a site-only tip with a route outranks them. For example, access-root-femoral-no-waveform ('Wire resistance: transduce the femoral sheath', phase ['femoral'] and route femoral, caution) scores 2.5 at the puncture, against 2 for a 'do' step tip. In the browser, a guided femoral case at the access workspace had st-elevation and chest-pain active (an ACS presentation). The phase-less PCI context took one of the 8 slots, and the acceptance tip access-femoral-scan-bifurcation came 8th of 8. Any further event, such as venous-flashback or hypotension, pushes it out, so the browser criterion is fragile.
findings.fix: Either set STEP_BONUS = 2 and correct the header text, or reserve the access slots at the access workspace with `CASE_TIP_LIMITS_AT_ACCESS = { perLab: { access: 8, diagnostic: 1, pci: 1, haemo: 1 }, total: 10 }`. Add a test that pins access-femoral-scan-bifurcation in shown(s, 'access') at the femoral puncture with an ACS indication (scenario or indication: 'STEMI') and an active patient event.

findings.problem: Two test titles claim more than the tests check. 'a needle through the back wall raises no-flashback; a sheath in the vein raises venous-flashback' never tests the flushSheath venous path (the raiseTip('venous-flashback') added in flushSheath has no test). 'raises declares every event, phase and route' checks phases and routes but not events.
findings.fix: Add a test that puts a femoral sheath into the vein (aim at the vein as the 'needle in the femoral vein' test does, run the wire, then removeNeedle, insertSheath and flushSheath), then expect activeEvents() to contain 'venous-flashback'. Or retitle the existing test. In the raises test, add `for (const e of c.events ?? []) expect(r.events, `${c.lab} ${e}`).toContain(e);` for sessions without a scenario.

findings.problem: Design 'lessonAndCaseLinks' says the debrief lists the tips shown (session.tipsShown). The session records them and SessionSummary.tipsShown carries them, but no screen shows them. Separately, LabTipsPanel's button reads 'Read the lesson', not 'Open lesson', and 'Ask for a tip', not 'Ask the attending'. The builder reported both points correctly as out of scope.
findings.fix: Out of scope: a follow-up package that owns HandoverPanel.tsx or the case debrief should list SessionSummary.tipsShown with TIP_BY_ID titles and an openLesson(lessonId) link. The owner of src/ui/lab/LabTipsPanel.tsx should add an optional askLabel prop, which CaseTipsPanel then passes as 'Ask the attending'.

findings.where: src/content/lab/raisable/waiting.ts; docs/realism/facts; src/simulation/access/site.ts and route.ts; src/simulation/session/scenarios/
findings.problem: These items are outside this package's files and the builder reported each one. 85 waiting entries are now ready but not yet retargeted. MP_TIPS.sampleS and MP_TIPS.spasmLevel are not yet in docs/realism/facts. access-central-vein-no-blood cannot be reached in the full case (no jugular or subclavian site), so criterion 5 is only partly met: that tip is shown only with a hand-made route 'jugular' context. The two cold-leg tips need limb-ischaemia, which only a scenario script raises.
findings.fix: Out of scope. Pass these to tip-retarget-catchup (waiting.ts), the facts owner (MODEL PARAMETER entries for MP_TIPS), access-venous (jugular and subclavian sites) and a full-case scenario that scripts limb-ischaemia. Record criterion 5 as partly met.

findings.problem: The simulation layer now has value imports from src/ui/lab. Both modules are framework-free with type-only imports, so there is no cycle or React dependency. The layering is still inverted, and it ties the session to UI-folder files that other packages edit.
findings.fix: Accept for now. In a later foundation package, move eventLog.ts and patientEvents.ts to src/simulation/lab/ and leave re-exports in src/ui/lab, so existing imports keep working.

rejected: Finding 7 (HandoverPanel debrief list of tipsShown; LabTipsPanel 'Open lesson' / 'Ask the attending' labels): not rejected on substance, but out of scope. HandoverPanel.tsx and src/ui/lab/LabTipsPanel.tsx are not this package's files. Needs a follow-up: list SessionSummary.tipsShown with TIP_BY_ID titles and an openLesson link in the debrief, and add an askLabel prop to LabTipsPanel that CaseTipsPanel would pass as 'Ask the attending'.

Finding 8 (waiting.ts retargets, MP_TIPS facts entries, jugular/subclavian sites, a limb-ischaemia full-case scenario): out of scope, as the reviewer says. Pass to tip-retarget-catchup (85 ready waiting entries), the facts owner (MODEL PARAMETER entries for MP_TIPS.sampleS and MP_TIPS.spasmLevel in docs/realism/facts), access-venous (jugular and subclavian sites for access-central-vein-no-blood) and a scenario package that scripts limb-ischaemia in the full case. Criterion 5 is partly met.

Finding 9 (caseSession importing EventLog and PatientEventAdapter from src/ui/lab): accepted as is, as the reviewer suggests. Both modules are framework-free. A later foundation package should move them to src/simulation/lab/ and leave re-exports in src/ui/lab.

fix.notes:
I checked every finding against the code and applied findings 1 to 6. Only package files were edited: /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/access/caseTips.ts, src/ui/access/caseTips.test.ts and src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts. CaseTipsPanel.tsx and ProcedureLab.tsx did not need changes.

1 (major, site leak), confirmed: tipsFor on the radial table context returns access-sheath-ooze-upsize. I added a site filter, fitsSite(), in caseTips.ts. In any access context with a route, a tip that names the femoral or radial site phase is shown only if it names the route's site. caseTipScore now applies it next to fitsStep. There is no exemption for 'plan', so access-planning-hostile-groin no longer appears in a radial case. The header comment explains the rule.
Tests: femoralOnly now also catches femoral-only site phases, and there is a matching radialOnly. everyMatch now uses the panel's own scoring (caseTipScore over LAB_TIPS), so the radial walk-through is checked on both shown and everyMatch. A new test covers the radial arm-perforation session: ooze-upsize matches under tipsFor but is absent from the table's shown tips and everyMatch, hostile-groin is absent at the chart, and no femoral-only tip appears in any workspace. A new fitsSite unit test covers both directions, including access-radial-spasm-no-traction in femoral closure and complication contexts.

2, confirmed: the radial-spasm event no longer comes from the 1-second sampling of wire.spasm. It is raised in commandWire on a non-zero move in a radial case with spasm at or above MP_TIPS.spasmLevel. I made the same change in commandCatheter, since the removed sampled check also covered a catheter in the arm. The doc comments for the event and for MP_TIPS were updated. New test: with the wire and catheter in the arm and the hidden level at 0.95, waiting raises nothing; a wire move raises the event.

3, applied: passBackWall is renamed passHadFlash. It is reset on each skin pass and set whenever the hub shows a flashback. no-flashback is raised when a flashback seen earlier on the pass has stopped. The no-lumen wire raise is unchanged. The back-wall test now also checks that a needle short of the artery, with no blood yet, raises nothing.

4, applied: the adapter's contrastHigh now compares (engine total + labTotals.contrastMl) / max(1, macdMl) with PATIENT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS.contrastFraction. This matches how refreshTotals adds up the case totals. New test: returnFromLab with 0.9 x macdMl raises high-contrast-volume.

5, applied both options: STEP_BONUS is now 2, so a step tip with no event scores at least 3 and a site-only tip at most 2.5. The header now says this holds among tips no event brought up. CASE_TIP_LIMITS_AT_ACCESS.total is now 10, so the other labs add to the 8 access slots instead of displacing them. New test: a femoral STEMI puncture with hypotension held keeps access-femoral-scan-bifurcation and access-needle-flashback-check in the panel, and among tips with no event the step tips come before the site-only ones.

6, applied: the existing test is retitled. A new test puts a sheath in the femoral vein, lets the needle event lapse, then flushSheath and checks for venous-flashback. The raises test now also checks events, using sessions that have events (a STEMI case and an arm perforation) and asserts that at least one event is active.

__caseSession.tips() is async, as reported. It returns mode, visible, workspace, stage, step, events, contexts, ids and shown.

Checked how session.tipsShown reaches the debrief: SessionSummary.tipsShown is filled, but nothing renders or logs it. logCase in useProcedureStore.ts does not pass it, HandoverPanel's SummaryBlock lists only the per-decision ledger tips, and no host passes tipsShown to the Debrief component.

problems.where: src/ui/access/panels/HandoverPanel.tsx (SummaryBlock) and src/state/useProcedureStore.ts (logCase); neither is in this package's file list
problems.problem: The plan's lesson and case links say 'the debrief lists tips shown (session.tipsShown)'. The session records tipsShown and SessionSummary.tipsShown is filled, but the end-of-case summary never shows that list. logCase also does not pass it into the run or logbook record, so the mentor Debrief's tipsShownOf() never sees the case's tips. The builder did not report this as out of scope.
problems.fix: Owner of HandoverPanel: in SummaryBlock, render sum.tipsShown as a 'Tips shown' list, each entry with the tip's title from useTipsModule().TIP_BY_ID and an 'Open lesson' link through openLesson(tip.lessonId). Owner of useProcedureStore: in logCase, emit one TIP_SHOWN_TELEMETRY ('lab.tip') event per id in sum.tipsShown on the run, with data {tipId}, or add the ids to the run's finish payload, so Debrief and tipsShownOf pick them up. Both are other packages' files: route this to them, not to proc-tip-context.

problems.where: src/ui/access/caseTips.ts, caseTipContexts for workspace 'access' when accessStep().step is null
problems.problem: Once the femoral sheath is flushed, the access workspace context drops to {lab:'access', phase:'femoral'} with no step. The panel then mixes tips from every femoral stage: access-planning-hostile-groin (planning), access-femoral-repuncture-wrong-height (wire), access-root-femoral-no-waveform and access-crossover-anticoagulated-care, instead of what applies once the sheath is in.
problems.fix: In caseTipContexts, when the workspace is 'access', step is null, the sheath is in and closure is not done, report phase 'sheath' with the site (as the table workspace already does). That gives {lab:'access', phase:'sheath', phases:[site], route}. After closure, report 'closure'.

problems.where: Tip content outside this package: access-femoral-repuncture-wrong-height, access-crossover-anticoagulated-care, access-femoral-deep-move-caudal (when: {phase:['femoral']}), access-root-femoral-no-waveform (when: {phase:['femoral'], route:['femoral']}), and radial equivalents such as access-radial-wire-resists, access-radial-heparin-timing, access-radial-thin-sheath-vasodilator
problems.problem: These tips are tagged with the site only, so the step filter cannot remove them. They fill the access cap at the puncture. The gap is real, but closing it inside this package would mean inventing a cause the full case does not model. caseSession.ts has no femoral artery size (the profile has only radialDiamMm), no plug or thrombus in the lumen and no embolus, so the nurse could only report a cold leg from something invented. Any incidence, dwell time or sheath-to-artery threshold would need a MODEL PARAMETER entry in docs/realism/facts, which is outside this package's files. The plan also gives the cause to other packages. access-closure-femoral-devices has a plug tamped before resistance in 'plug-deep-sheath' raise limb-ischaemia, and its tipIntegration names access-closure-cold-leg; it also lists caseSession.ts and may be editing it now. access-cx-endovascular-control's tipIntegration names both cold-leg tips with limb-ischaemia and declares raises in src/simulation/session/modules/endovascular.ts, which the reach test already reads. Adding limb-ischaemia to CASE_SESSION_EVENTS with nothing that raises it would make the reachability report claim a tip is reachable when it is not. Option B (outOfScope) is the right fix: the owner of src/content/lab/raisable/waiting.ts (found-tip-retarget / tip-retarget-catchup) should move access-cx-cold-leg-six-ps to access-cx-endovascular-control and access-closure-cold-leg to access-closure-femoral-devices (or both to endovascular), and record the move in docs/curriculum/lab-build-plan.json.
